title: Micro-scaled Macronutrient Extraction from Invertebrates
author: Jordan P Cuff
materials: Lyse the tissue and ensure it is mixed/homogenous. Lysis can be carried out using a pestle and mortar, or bead-beating method, ensuring all available tissue is taken forward and any beads added are removed. If using a bead-beating method (e.g. Qiagen Tissuelyser II at 30 Hz for 8 min), it may be easier to do so in a liquid matrix, so you can do this after the initial addition of NaOH in the next step. Care must be taken to avoid contact with NaOH when doing so.

steps.title: Collect and kill specimens
steps.instruction: Collect invertebrates and kill them (e.g., by freezing). If specimens are fluid‑preserved, transfer the whole material including preservative into a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube or 2 ml screw‑top tube; evaporate the preservative later during drying.

steps.title: Desiccate specimens
steps.instruction: Desiccate the specimens either by freeze‑drying (preferred) or by heat‑drying at 60 °C for 24–48 h (shorter if using a heated centrifuge with vacuum). Avoid burning or damaging the bodies.

steps.title: Weigh dried specimens
steps.instruction: If possible, weigh the dried specimen (or the tube + precipitate for fluid‑preserved samples) on a highly sensitive balance and record the mass for later normalisation.

steps.title: First chloroform‑methanol extraction
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl of 1:12 chloroform : methanol to each tube, seal, and incubate at room temperature for 24 h.

steps.title: Separate lipid fraction
steps.instruction: Remove 400 µl of the chloroform : methanol solution and place it in a separate, airtight glass tube (or other chloroform‑compatible container) for lipid analysis; keep the remaining solution in the original tube for later protein‑carbohydrate work.

steps.title: Prepare lipid standards
steps.instruction: Make a stock dilution series of a lipid analogue (e.g., analytical lard oil) in 1:12 chloroform : methanol at concentrations 0, 12.5, 62.5, 125, 250, 375, 500, 750 and 1000 µg ml⁻¹ (nine points). Verify plastic compatibility if heating the solvent.

steps.title: Prepare vanillin reagent
steps.instruction: For each sample/standard repeat prepare the following (overage included): 275 µg vanillin, 46 µl hot water, 183 µl 85 % phosphoric acid.

steps.title: Evaporate lipid samples
steps.instruction: Pipette three replicates of 50 µl of each lipid standard or sample into a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate; heat at 100 °C in a ventilated hood until solvent evaporates (≈5–10 min).

steps.title: Add sulfuric acid
steps.instruction: Add 15 µl concentrated H₂SO₄ to each well, vortex/mix, and incubate again at 100 °C for 15 min while monitoring the plate closely.

steps.title: Develop vanillin colour
steps.instruction: Cool plates to room temperature, add 200 µl vanillin reagent to each well, vortex/mix, and let stand 5 min.

steps.title: Transfer to fresh plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µl from each well to a new 96‑well plate to avoid warped wells or particulates.

steps.title: Measure lipid absorbance
steps.instruction: Read absorbance at 490 nm with a spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Second chloroform‑methanol extraction
steps.instruction: From the original tube, discard ~100 µl supernatant (avoid tissue), add another 500 µl of 1:12 chloroform : methanol, and incubate at room temperature for 24 h to remove residual lipids.

steps.title: Evaporate residual solvent
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant (avoid tissue) and evaporate any remaining solvent completely.

steps.title: Alkaline digestion
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl 0.1 M NaOH to the tube, then incubate at 80 °C for 30 min in a thermoshaker.

steps.title: Overnight soak (optional)
steps.instruction: Allow the tube to sit at room temperature overnight; this step can be omitted if tissue is already fully lysed (e.g., by sonication).

steps.title: Centrifuge extracts
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 10 min at 13 000 rpm.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer 400 µl of the clear supernatant to a fresh tube; this will be used for both carbohydrate and protein assays.

steps.title: Prepare carbohydrate standards
steps.instruction: Create a starch dilution series in purified water at 0, 0.25, 1.25, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 15 and 20 µg ml⁻¹ (nine points, covering 0–0.02 mg ml⁻¹). Adjust range if needed for other taxa.

steps.title: Prepare anthrone reagent
steps.instruction: Prepare anthrone reagent according to the protocol (amounts per repeat are given in the original method; use reagent overage for triplicates).

steps.title: Run anthrone assay
steps.instruction: Pipette three replicates of 40 µl of each carbohydrate standard or sample into a 96‑well plate, add 140 µl anthrone reagent, vortex/mix, incubate at 92 °C in a ventilated hood for 30 min, cool to room temperature, then incubate an additional 30 min before reading.

steps.title: Prepare protein standards
steps.instruction: Make a BSA dilution series in purified water at 0, 12.5, 62.5, 125, 250, 375, 500, 750 and 1000 µg ml⁻¹ (nine points, 0–1 mg ml⁻¹). Adjust if required.

steps.title: Run Lowry protein assay
steps.instruction: Add three replicates of 40 µl of each protein standard or sample to a 96‑well plate, add 200 µl Modified Lowry Reagent, vortex/mix, incubate at 20–25 °C for 10 min, add 20 µl 1X (1 N) Folin‑Ciocalteu reagent, vortex/mix, incubate at 20–25 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Measure protein absorbance
steps.instruction: Read absorbance at 750 nm (and additionally at 620 nm if required) with a spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Calculate concentrations
steps.instruction: Convert absorbance values to concentrations using the appropriate standard curves; because only 500 µl extraction volume was used, divide calculated mg ml⁻¹ values by two to obtain whole‑body macronutrient content, and correct for any further dilutions made during the assays.
